chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from Yunus ibn Abdul Rahman, from Dawud ibn Zurbi, who said:

I fell sick in Medina with a severe illness, so that reached Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He wrote to me: 'Your illness has reached me, so buy a Sa' of wheat, then lie on your back and scatter it upon your chest however it scatters, and say:'

O Allah, I ask You by Your Name which, when the desperate one asks You with it, You remove the harm from him, and grant him authority in the earth, and make him Your vicegerent over Your creatures, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You grant me health from my illness.
Then sit up, gather the wheat from around you, and say the like of that, and distribute it, a Mudd to each poor person, and say the like of that.
Dawud said: So I did that, and it was as if I had been released from a shackle, and not just one person did it, and he benefited from it.

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication and ritual for curing illness according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia tradition of combining spiritual supplication with tangible acts of charity (sadaqah) for healing, where Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes scattering wheat while invoking God's name to remove affliction. The practice emphasizes the interconnectedness of physical recovery and social welfare, as the wheat is subsequently distributed to the poor, reinforcing the merit of giving in times of distress. This method reflects the broader theological principle that divine healing is often mediated through both divine decree and human agency, including the distribution of sustenance to the needy.
